title: Autonomous version rollback circuitry for private control plane upgrades
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: Private (VPC) control plane upgrades occasionally encounter latent incompatibilities (operator API changes, CRD drift, or subtle reconciliation regressions) that pass initial smoke checks but surface under production tenant load. When that happens we need fast, automated, and low-blast-radius rollback behavior that is: deterministic, observable, and safe across Terraform-managed infra and the control-plane deployment graph.

Objective: Implement an "autonomous rollback circuitry" that detects canary degradations (via application-level and infra-level signals), isolates affected tenants, and performs an automated rollback of the control plane version while preserving state and minimizing tenant impact. The system should be usable for both Hosted-private and On-prem packages and integrate with existing Terraform modules and the control-plane operator.

Scope / Non-Goals:
- In scope: canary promotion orchestration, multi-signal health gating, automated rollback executor (safe variant), Terraform plan/apply adapters to pin versions, and alerting/forensics artifacts.
- Out of scope: fully replacing manual approval for enterprise legal/large customers (we will instead surface an opt-in flag).

Success criteria / Acceptance criteria:
1) Canary cohort promotion script can be configured with fractional tenant fractions and promote/demote automatically based on defined SLOs.
2) Rollback executor can revert control-plane artifacts to the last known-good release with <5 minute RTO for canary cohort and <30 minute RTO for global rollback (timings under typical infra).
3) Rollback produces an audit bundle: terraform plan diff, operator reconcile logs, and telemetry snapshot stored to S3/Drive link.
4) No data loss for CRD-backed resources (we validate with staged PR and replay tests).
5) Module changes are backwards compatible for customers on pinned-version workflows.

High-level design:
- Detection signals: composite gating using (a) control-plane health probes (reconcile loop errors, restarts), (b) API latency (p50/p95/p99), (c) request-level error rates from ingress + operator-side errors, and (d) tenant-facing anomalies (consumer-reported 5xx spike).
- SLO rules: configurable thresholds with hysteresis windows (default: p95 API latency +20% vs baseline OR error-rate >1% sustained over 3 minutes OR reconcile error spikes >5x baseline).
- Isolation: when a canary cohort trips, traffic is automatically shifted away from canary nodes using our in-cluster traffic-siphon controller (mirror/siphon approach) and those tenants are marked as "quarantined" in the control-plane metadata store.
- Rollback executor: a two-phase safe rollback: 1) fast rollforward to a fallback image tag for operator (if available) OR 2) terraform-driven version pin revert that updates control-plane version variables and applies a controlled terraform plan with apply-time health gates.
- Safety nets: preflight dry-run, safe-mode that performs a shadow apply (no data-destructive ops), and automatic pause on any failing health-probe during rollback.
- Observability: sliceable dashboards per-cohort with synthetic canaries, per-tenant traces, and an auto-generated incident doc (playbook) containing terraform plan diff, git tags, PRs, and key metrics snapshot.

Terraform/IaC changes (engineering notes):
- Add "version-rollover" module (non-breaking) that exposes an output: last_known_good_version and supports a fast-revert toggle.
- Introduce plan-time hooks to capture terraform plan json and upload to artifacts-bucket for audit.
- Provide an apply wrapper (redwood-ctl apply-safe) which can perform a plan, validate health gates via a webhook to the control-plane canary-service, and then apply only when health gates pass.

Operational playbook (outline):
1) Stage: create a canary cohort (2-5% tenant fraction) via terraform variable change + orchestration.
2) Monitor: composite gate watches telemetry for 15 minutes.
3) If degrade: invoke isolation (siphon) and trigger automated rollback executor.
4) Post-rollback: run reconciliation smoke tests and release the cohort back after manual review (unless auto-approve enabled).

Compatibility and migration:
- Default behavior is opt-in (customers must enable autonomous rollback in their private config).
- For pinned-version customers, we expose an operator flag that disables auto rollback and instead generates a prepopulated incident bundle for manual approval.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Risk: false positives could unnecessarily rollback healthy versions; mitigations include multi-signal voting and gradual thresholds with cooldown.
- Risk: terraform reverts may interact poorly with state drift (operator-managed resources vs terraform-managed); mitigation: use shadow plan and explicit state lock + operator reconciliation pre-checks.
- Trade-off: faster RTO vs blast radius; we prioritize cohort-first rollback (lowest blast radius) with global fallback if cohort rollback fails.

Open decisions: (see comments for timeline)
- Should rollback executor change operator CRs or change helm image tags? (engineering preferred: image tag revert + CR compatibility shim)
- Where to store the audit bundles (S3 vs internal Drive)? (pref S3 with Drive link mirror)
- Default thresholds for SLO gating (need product + SRE input).
